questions.q: A 35-year-old woman presents with a 6-month history of erythematous plaques with silvery scales on her elbows, knees, and scalp. Nail examination reveals pitting and onycholysis. Which cytokine is most centrally involved in the pathogenesis of this condition?
questions.exp: Psoriasis is a Th17-driven disease. IL-17A (produced by Th17 cells) is the key effector cytokine driving keratinocyte proliferation and neutrophil recruitment. Biologics targeting IL-17 (secukinumab, ixekizumab) are highly effective.

questions.q: A 22-year-old male presents with multiple painless punched-out ulcers on his penis, associated with bilateral non-tender inguinal lymphadenopathy. Dark-field microscopy of the ulcer exudate shows motile spiral organisms. What is the most appropriate first-line treatment?
opts: Benzathine penicillin G 2.4 MU IM single dose
questions.exp: Primary syphilis (Treponema pallidum) presents with a painless chancre and non-tender lymphadenopathy. Benzathine penicillin G 2.4 MU IM as a single dose is the treatment of choice for primary, secondary, and early latent syphilis.

questions.q: A 28-year-old farmer from Bihar presents with hypopigmented anaesthetic macules on his trunk and thickened greater auricular nerve. Slit-skin smear shows acid-fast bacilli with a bacterial index of 3+. What is the WHO classification for this patient?
questions.exp: WHO classifies leprosy as multibacillary (MB) when there are more than 5 skin lesions OR any positive slit-skin smear. A BI of 3+ confirms MB leprosy. MB treatment: rifampicin, clofazimine, dapsone for 12 months.

questions.q: A 45-year-old diabetic patient presents with an itchy scaly rash in the groin with a well-defined, raised border and central clearing. KOH mount shows branching hyphae. The causative organism most commonly responsible for this presentation in India is:
questions.exp: Tinea cruris (ringworm of groin) is most commonly caused by Trichophyton rubrum in India, followed by Epidermophyton floccosum. T. rubrum has overtaken E. floccosum as the predominant cause in recent decades.

questions.q: A 60-year-old woman develops painful grouped vesicles along the right T5 dermatome, preceded by 3 days of pain and paresthesia. She develops post-herpetic neuralgia. Which mechanism best explains the persistence of pain after lesion healing?
opts: Ongoing viral replication in sensory ganglia
questions.exp: Post-herpetic neuralgia results from central sensitization, neuroinflammation, and damage to primary afferent nociceptors from VZV reactivation. Changes in dorsal horn processing maintain pain long after viral clearance.

questions.q: A 55-year-old man presents with tense bullae on normal-appearing and erythematous skin, predominantly on the flexural areas and trunk. Direct immunofluorescence shows linear IgG and C3 along the basement membrane zone. The target antigen is:
questions.exp: Bullous pemphigoid (BP) targets BP180 (BPAG2/collagen XVII) and BP230 (BPAG1) in the hemidesmosome. Linear IgG/C3 at the BMZ on DIF is characteristic. Tense bullae on flexures in elderly is the classic presentation.

questions.q: A 40-year-old woman with SLE presents with a butterfly rash, photosensitivity, and oral ulcers. Her ANA is positive (1:1280), anti-dsDNA is elevated, and complement levels are low. Which skin finding on histology is most characteristic of lupus?
opts: Vacuolar degeneration of basal layer with thickened PAS-positive BMZ and interface change
questions.exp: Lupus histology shows vacuolar degeneration of basal keratinocytes, thickened PAS-positive BMZ, and perivascular/periadnexal lymphocytic infiltrate. DIF (lupus band test) shows IgG, IgM, IgA, and complement deposited at the DEJ. The combination is characteristic of lupus.

questions.q: A 30-year-old male presents with a solitary painless ulcer on his glans penis with indurated edges. He reports unprotected sexual intercourse 3 weeks ago. Tzanck smear is negative. VDRL is non-reactive. What should be the next step?
opts: Treat empirically for syphilis and repeat VDRL after 2 weeks
Start antiviral therapy for genital herpes
questions.exp: VDRL may be non-reactive in early primary syphilis (seronegative window period). A painless indurated ulcer is highly characteristic of syphilis. Empirical treatment with benzathine penicillin should be given, and VDRL repeated in 2-4 weeks to confirm seroconversion.

questions.q: A 25-year-old leprosy patient on MDT develops sudden erythema and tenderness of pre-existing skin lesions, with fever and joint pain, but no new nerve damage. This reaction is best classified as:
questions.exp: Erythema nodosum leprosum (ENL/Type 2 reaction) occurs in MB leprosy (LL/BL) as immune complex-mediated (Type III hypersensitivity). It presents with tender erythematous nodules, fever, and systemic symptoms. Treatment is thalidomide or prednisolone.

questions.q: A 70-year-old man presents with a pearly, translucent nodule with telangiectasia on his sun-exposed nose. It has been slowly enlarging over 2 years. Biopsy shows palisading basaloid cells with peripheral clefting. What is the most likely diagnosis?
questions.exp: Basal cell carcinoma (BCC) is the most common skin cancer in fair-skinned individuals. Nodular BCC shows palisading basaloid cells with peripheral retraction artifact (clefting) on histology. UV radiation is the main risk factor.

questions.q: A 32-year-old woman presents with Raynaud phenomenon, puffy hands, and heartburn for 8 months. On examination, she has sclerodactyly and telangiectasias on her face. Which antibody is most specific for systemic sclerosis with limited cutaneous involvement?
questions.exp: Anti-centromere antibodies (ACA) are highly specific for limited cutaneous systemic sclerosis (lcSSc/CREST syndrome), associated with a better prognosis. Anti-Scl-70 is associated with diffuse cutaneous SSc and pulmonary fibrosis.

questions.q: A 20-year-old male presents with flaccid bullae that rupture easily, leaving raw erosions on the scalp, face, and trunk. Nikolsky sign is positive. DIF shows intercellular IgG deposits in the epidermis. The target antigen is most likely:
questions.exp: Pemphigus vulgaris targets desmoglein 3 (in mucosal disease) and both Dsg3 + Dsg1 (in mucocutaneous disease). Pemphigus foliaceus targets only Dsg1. The 'tombstone' pattern on DIF represents IgG binding to desmosomal proteins throughout the epidermis.

questions.q: A 3-year-old child presents with honey-crusted erosions around the mouth and nose. The causative organism predominantly responsible for non-bullous impetigo in India is:
questions.exp: While traditionally Group A Streptococcus was the classic cause of non-bullous impetigo, S. aureus has emerged as the predominant organism in both bullous and non-bullous impetigo in most regions including India. Bullous impetigo is always caused by phage group II S. aureus producing exfoliative toxin.

questions.q: A 50-year-old male presents with progressive thickening and yellowing of all toenails with transverse ridging. KOH mount from subungual debris shows septate hyphae with arthroconidia. The drug with the highest mycological cure rate for onychomycosis is:
questions.exp: Terbinafine (allylamine) has the highest mycological and clinical cure rates for toenail onychomycosis (predominantly dermatophyte). It is fungicidal via inhibition of squalene epoxidase. Duration is 12 weeks for toenails, 6 weeks for fingernails.

questions.q: A 28-year-old HIV-positive man with CD4 count of 80 cells/μL presents with painful perianal ulcers present for more than 1 month despite standard antiviral therapy. PCR confirms HSV-2 infection. This presentation meets criteria for which AIDS-defining condition?
questions.exp: Chronic mucocutaneous herpes simplex (ulcers persisting >1 month) is an AIDS-defining illness. In severely immunocompromised patients, HSV can cause severe, persistent ulcers requiring IV acyclovir or foscarnet if acyclovir-resistant.

questions.q: A 45-year-old patient undergoes Mohs micrographic surgery for a recurrent BCC on the nose. What is the primary advantage of Mohs surgery over wide local excision?
opts: Maximum tissue conservation with complete margin assessment
questions.exp: Mohs micrographic surgery offers the highest cure rates (up to 99% for primary BCC) through complete circumferential peripheral and deep margin assessment (CCPDMA), allowing maximum tissue conservation. It is the gold standard for recurrent, large, or functionally/cosmetically critical site tumours.

questions.q: A 35-year-old woman with chronic plaque psoriasis involving 40% BSA is on methotrexate for 3 years. Liver biopsy shows periportal fibrosis (Grade IIIA). The recommended action is:
opts: Discontinue methotrexate and switch to a biologic
questions.exp: Roenigk classification Grade IIIA (periportal fibrosis) is an indication to discontinue methotrexate. The cumulative dose threshold for liver biopsy is traditionally 1-1.5g. Biologics (TNF-α inhibitors, IL-17/IL-23 inhibitors) are appropriate alternatives.

questions.q: A 25-year-old presents with well-defined hypopigmented patches with fine scaling on the chest and back. Wood's lamp shows golden-yellow fluorescence. KOH mount reveals short curved hyphae and round yeast cells. The causative agent is:
questions.exp: Pityriasis versicolor is caused by Malassezia furfur (and related species). The pathognomonic KOH finding is short curved hyphae and yeast cells ('spaghetti and meatballs'). Wood's lamp shows yellow-green fluorescence due to pityriacitrin produced by the organism.

questions.q: A 48-year-old woman presents with muscle weakness, heliotrope rash, and Gottron's papules on her knuckles. Which investigation is most critical to perform immediately?
questions.exp: Dermatomyositis (DM) in adults has a 15-25% association with internal malignancy (most commonly ovarian, lung, GI, breast cancers). Screening for underlying malignancy is the most critical immediate step. Investigations include CT chest/abdomen/pelvis, PET scan, and age-appropriate cancer screening.

questions.q: A 19-year-old presents with multiple soft, flesh-colored papules with central umbilication on the face and trunk. He is immunocompetent. Which virus is responsible?
questions.exp: Molluscum contagiosum is caused by Molluscum contagiosum virus (MCV), a poxvirus. Central umbilication and Henderson-Paterson bodies (molluscum bodies) in the cytoplasm of infected keratinocytes are characteristic. In immunocompetent individuals, it is self-limiting.

questions.q: A 65-year-old man presents with a rapidly growing, firm, flesh-colored nodule on his forearm that appeared over 6 weeks. Histology shows a central keratin-filled crater with well-differentiated squamous epithelium. The most likely diagnosis is:
questions.exp: Keratoacanthoma (KA) is a rapidly growing squamoproliferative tumour with classic crateriform architecture and central keratin plug. It is now considered a variant of well-differentiated SCC. Treatment is excision. Rapid growth over weeks followed by potential spontaneous resolution helps distinguish it clinically.

questions.q: A patient with lepromatous leprosy on MDT develops sudden onset of erythematous, edematous nodules on the face and upper limbs with high fever. Biopsy shows leukocytoclastic vasculitis. The BEST treatment for this condition is:
questions.exp: Thalidomide is the drug of choice for ENL (erythema nodosum leprosum), particularly recurrent/severe cases. It acts by inhibiting TNF-α. Prednisolone is the alternative when thalidomide is contraindicated (e.g., women of childbearing age). Clofazimine has anti-inflammatory properties but slower onset.

questions.q: A 30-year-old presents with atopic dermatitis unresponsive to topical steroids and tacrolimus. She is started on dupilumab. What is the primary mechanism of action of dupilumab?
opts: Blocks IL-4Rα subunit shared by IL-4 and IL-13 receptors
questions.exp: Dupilumab is a fully human monoclonal antibody targeting the IL-4Rα receptor subunit shared by both IL-4 and IL-13 signaling pathways, the key drivers of Th2 inflammation in atopic dermatitis. It is the first biologic approved for moderate-severe AD.

questions.q: A 5-year-old child develops high fever followed by diffuse erythema of the skin and desquamation around the mouth and nose. Nikolsky sign is positive. Biopsy shows intraepidermal cleavage at the granular layer. The exfoliative toxin responsible acts on which target?
questions.exp: Staphylococcal scalded skin syndrome (SSSS) is caused by exfoliative toxins (ET-A, ET-B) produced by phage group II S. aureus. These serine proteases specifically cleave desmoglein 1, causing superficial blistering in the granular layer. Unlike TEN, the cleavage is intraepidermal.

questions.q: Which of the following correctly describes the cleavage plane and direct immunofluorescence findings in dermatitis herpetiformis?
opts: Intraepidermal cleavage; IgG at DEJ in linear pattern
Subepidermal cleavage; IgA deposits in dermal papillae in granular pattern
Subepidermal cleavage; IgG linear along BMZ
questions.exp: Dermatitis herpetiformis (DH) is associated with gluten-sensitive enteropathy. Subepidermal vesicles form at dermal papillary tips. DIF shows granular IgA deposits in dermal papillae (pathognomonic). Target antigen is epidermal transglutaminase (TG3). Treatment: dapsone + gluten-free diet.

questions.q: A 40-year-old presents with a pearly white plaque on the lateral border of the tongue that cannot be wiped off. HIV ELISA is positive with CD4 of 180. Biopsy shows koilocytes with beading of nuclear chromatin. The causative agent is:
questions.exp: Oral hairy leukoplakia (OHL) is caused by Epstein-Barr virus (EBV) reactivation in immunosuppressed individuals. It cannot be scraped off (unlike candidiasis). Histology shows koilocytes, beading of nuclei, and hair-like surface projections. It is an indicator of immune compromise.

questions.q: A 55-year-old woman presents with a darkly pigmented lesion on her palm with irregular borders, variegated color, and diameter of 12mm. Dermoscopy shows irregular parallel ridge pattern. The most appropriate initial management is:
opts: Punch biopsy of the most pigmented area
Topical imiquimod and review in 3 months
questions.exp: Acral lentiginous melanoma (ALM) presents on the palms, soles, and nail units. Irregular parallel ridge pattern on dermoscopy is a red flag. Excisional biopsy with narrow margins (2mm) is preferred for initial diagnosis to obtain full histological depth (Breslow thickness) for staging.

questions.q: A 28-year-old pregnant woman (32 weeks) develops intensely pruritic urticarial papules and plaques starting in striae on the abdomen, classically sparing the periumbilical area. This condition is best described as:
opts: Pruritic urticarial papules and plaques of pregnancy (PUPPP)
questions.exp: PUPPP (now called polymorphic eruption of pregnancy) begins in abdominal striae and classically spares the periumbilical area. It occurs in the 3rd trimester, especially in primigravidas. DIF is negative. It is benign for mother and fetus; treatment is symptomatic.

questions.q: A patient undergoing patch testing for suspected contact dermatitis shows a +++ reaction (vesiculation, spreading beyond patch site) to potassium dichromate. This type of hypersensitivity reaction is classified as:
questions.exp: Allergic contact dermatitis is a classic Type IV (delayed-type) hypersensitivity reaction mediated by sensitized T lymphocytes (CD4+ Th1 cells, CD8+ cytotoxic cells). Sensitization occurs on first exposure; elicitation occurs 48-72 hours after re-exposure. Patch testing exploits this mechanism.

questions.q: A 22-year-old male presents with a painful genital ulcer with a soft, non-indurated base and necrotic floor. There is tender unilateral inguinal lymphadenopathy (bubo). Gram stain reveals 'school of fish' arrangement of gram-negative coccobacilli. The treatment of choice is:
questions.exp: Chancroid is caused by Haemophilus ducreyi. It presents with a painful, soft ulcer (vs painless in syphilis) and tender suppurative inguinal lymphadenopathy (bubo). Gram stain shows the 'school of fish' / 'railroad tracks' pattern. Treatment: azithromycin 1g single dose or ceftriaxone 250mg IM stat.

questions.q: A 16-year-old boy presents with chronic plaque psoriasis and is found to have HLA-Cw6 positivity. Regarding the genetics of psoriasis, which of the following is CORRECT?
opts: HLA-Cw6 is more strongly associated with late-onset psoriasis (Type II)
HLA-Cw6 is strongly associated with guttate psoriasis and early-onset psoriasis (Type I)
HLA-Cw6 confers protection against nail psoriasis
HLA-Cw6 is found in less than 5% of patients with psoriasis
questions.exp: HLA-Cw6 is the major genetic susceptibility allele for psoriasis, present in ~65% of patients with Type I (early-onset, familial) psoriasis and is strongly associated with guttate psoriasis triggered by streptococcal infection. Type II (late-onset, >40 years) has weaker HLA association. HLA-Cw6+ patients also have a better response to ustekinumab.
